newsitem.title: USA: NY state group urges Moynihan to drop stadium bill.
newsitem.headline: NY state group urges Moynihan to drop stadium bill.

text.p: Finance officers in New York State urged U.S. Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan to withdraw or soften his controversial bill to bar the use of tax exempt bonds for stadium financings.

In a September 9 letter to the New York Democrat, the New York State Government Finance Officers' Association said the bill's curb on local decisionmaking is unprecedented and that the measure's June 14, 1996 retroactive effective date is disrupting the tax-exempt bond market.

The letter, signed by association president Dominick Cafferillo, says Moynihan's bill would not only impact future facilities but bonds issued for capital improvements to existing stadiums and as part of refundings.
The group also said Moynihan's definition of professional sports facilities is too broad.
"We believe that, at a minimum, the definition should be restricted to major league sports facilities and should not include minor league and non-profit sports facilities," Cafferillo said.

Even if Moynihan intended to reach both professional and minor league facilities, the bill should not touch community stadiums that are only sometimes used by professional teams for minor league practice, Cafferillo said.

"We believe that the definition of professional sports facilities should exclude facilities that are primarily used by or benefit the local community and that provide only ancillary use to professional teams and organizations," he said.
A Moynihan aide said he had not yet seen the letter.
Moynihan introduced the measure on June 14.

Following a chorus of criticism from bond groups, he announced June 28 that he would add transition language to protect projects that are far along in financing. But he refused to drop the June 14 general effective date.
Moynihan aides met with state and local government groups July 11 to discuss groups' concerns with the bill. But, again, they did not pledge to revise the effective date.
